limitations: Reviewer is a separate AI agent session on the same host and the same operator account. A coordinator session of the producer side launched it. It is not a second machine, a second operator, or a human. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and read nothing outside the repository and the frozen code snapshot (commit a62527e) that the brief named.

This is the third review of this configuration by this reviewer id. The v1 packets (score 70.8) were rejected for four defects (readable connector schema keys; an invented edit action and result; two false native_absent states). The v2 packets (86.83) were approved on 2026-10-04. The v3 packets are a rebuild for the duplicate rule of 2026-10-05. This review is a delta review against v2: native/ and inputs/ of every v3 packet are byte-identical to v2; only manifest.json and seven runtime source files differ. The v2 findings on those bytes are carried over; the checks that the brief required were run again on v3. A defect that this reviewer cannot see may still exist.

The replay ran the scoring source that is inside each packet. The producer wrote that source. The packet copies of native_density.py and score_replay.py are older than the snapshot at commit a62527e: they do not hold the later restatement code. The reviewer ran the snapshot code on the public native bytes and got the same 10 occurrences of the same 8 events, so the later rule changes no row here. The reviewer wrote its own scripts (no session_bench import) for the event list, the occurrence count by content comparison, the byte recount, the digest oracle and the binding checks.

Compound shell calls. In each run the model made two Bash calls and no Edit call. Call 1 holds the inspect and baseline helpers, each followed by an exit echo. Call 2 holds a quoted heredoc write of checkout.py and the final helper with an exit echo. The split rule (rubric.md, Matching table) and its code were written on 2026-10-04, after the captures and after the first rejection. The reviewer confirmed from the public native bytes that each credited helper segment is in the command, each credited result is one line of the native tool result, and each exit code is the exit=N line directly after it. The projection adds only derived identifiers (parent tool id plus segment index) and a status derived from the exit code. The observer's edit action is named Edit; the native record is a shell write. They match by action kind, target and turn, not by tool name. The observer's edit action and its placeholder result (fixed text 'compound edit completed') are inferred by the finalize script from the GUI receipt and the file hashes; they are not observed tool events. The placeholder result stays unmatched, so work.results and causal.action_result are 3 of 4 and broad.event_timestamps is 11 of 13. These three shortfalls come from the model's choice of a heredoc write, not from a gap in the session format; a run that used the Edit tool would probably score 4 of 4. Vendor guidance from this row must say so.

Compound rule across rows. The v2 review reported that the rubric row had no '&&' inference while the Codex decoder had one. The rubric row in the snapshot now states the inference and the Claude decoder in the v3 packets applies it. It changes no row of this configuration (the Desktop commands use ';' with an exit echo). The reviewer did not re-score the Codex row.

Duplicate rule. The rule (rubric.md, Duplicate-safety read) was written on 2026-10-05, after the captures and after the v2 approval, and the owner applied it to every row. Effect on this row in each run: broad.naive_reader_duplicate_safety from 11 of 11 (3.0 points) to 6 of 10 (1.8 points); density from 4.52, 4.58, 4.44 percent to 4.36, 4.42, 4.27 percent; per-run score from about 86.83 to about 85.62. The other 29 metric rows are equal to v2 in every run.

Reviewer's own count on the raw records, public and private bytes, all three runs: 8 events (2 prompts, 2 assistant text messages, 2 Bash calls, 2 tool results) and 10 records that state them. Each prompt is stated twice in full: in a queue-operation enqueue record and in the user record after it. The dequeue record names no record and no field marks a copy as superseded. Every other event is stated by one record. wireToolInputs repeats the command inside the same assistant record, and toolUseResult.stdout repeats the result output inside the same user record; one record is one occurrence. last-prompt holds a cut prefix of the first prompt; custom-title holds other text; no attachment and no field of the Desktop metadata holds a prompt, a response, a call argument or a result output (checked on the private parent too).

Judgments in the duplicate count that the reviewer accepted. (a) The population is every event the read states, counted on raw records; one compound Bash call is one call event and one result event here, while the work metrics split it into segments. With the 13 observer events as the population the result would be 9 of 13 (about 2.08 points, 0.28 more). (b) The result record of the second call holds, inside its bashEditDiff of the benchmark's own helper ledger file, the two helper output lines of the first result in escaped form, but not the exit lines; by the written rule (full result output) it does not restate the first result. A looser reading would give 5 of 11 (about 1.36 points, 0.44 less). In run 2 the same record holds the new file body because the command printed it; it does not hold the command. (c) The read is the transcript and the Desktop metadata by the membership rule; the evidence text in the packet says 'the read is the transcript JSONL' and the counting code walks only the transcript. The reviewer checked by content comparison that the metadata adds no occurrence, so the number is the same. (d) The empty thinking record is not a message event.

Density. The reviewer recomputed useful and total bytes from the public bytes and got the packet values (20453 of 468767; 20748 of 469033; 20020 of 468316). The enqueue record keeps the user_message role, the user record that repeats the prompt is a snapshot, and no record that counts as a second occurrence is counted as useful. 42 transcript records per run (attachments and state records) keep the role unknown; they are in the denominator either way.

Digest rule. These packets were not rebuilt for the digest rule of 2026-10-05; their native/ and inputs/ bytes are those of v2. The reviewer ran check_public_packets from the snapshot: 555 public-byte digests, 3 replay outputs, 51 allowlisted occurrences, none unbound; without the allowlist it reports 33 unbound occurrences. Allowlist reasons judged: the screenshot digest is sound (private image bytes). The damaged-package decode_manifest_sha256 is sound: the reviewer confirmed that it is the SHA-256 of a 200-byte manifest that holds the SHA-256 of the private transcript without one response line, and that this transcript differs from the public one in about 298,000 bytes on 41 lines and holds 7 random identifiers that are not public; a guessed home name or e-mail cannot be confirmed through it. The inventory metadata_digest reason is plausible but not verified: the tool that computed it is not in the repository, and the reviewer relies on the receipt text (metadata of about 4,500 files) and on the fact that the four values chain across the runs.

work.changed_files hashes are rebuilt from native bytes: the pre-image is checkout_source in the native inspect result of turn 1, the post-image is the heredoc body of call 2, and the bashEditDiff of the same result turns the first into the second (one hunk over the whole file). Both equal the observer pair. The transcript stores no file hash for the edit itself.

broad.stable_root_location is measured from a derivation rule, not from an observed path. The retained inventories recorded no source path for the two selected files. The verifier requires: metadata-only before and after inventories with exactly 2 new files, one session id in both files, Desktop cwd equal to originCwd and the first transcript cwd, every native timestamp inside the run's inventory window, and no overlap of the three windows. The reviewer re-checked these on the public bytes (margins 11 to 12 s before and 30 to 36 s after; file counts chain 4511, 4513, 4515, 4517) and mutation-tested the verifier. This evidence is weaker than the observed-path receipts of the Codex CLI and Claude CLI rows. The path pattern was confirmed only on later private captures of CLI 2.1.286, not on 2.1.270, and the reviewer did not repeat that check in this review. The account and organisation directory names are blanked, so a public reader cannot check every variable of the locator.

Runs 1 and 2 are corrective attempts (correction-1). Their originals are recorded as invalid captures with reason controller_did_not_preserve_per_run_filesystem_observer_before_fixture_reset; they produced no score, and their GUI receipts show the same visible outcome as the corrections. The reason does not depend on the result. The corrections ran 5 to 8 minutes after run 3 on the same build with a prompt that declares the correction. The rubric says not to replace a scheduled run with a corrective attempt. No owner decision that accepts these two runs is on record in the handover at the time of this review. The retained attempt.json files still say state running and score_eligible false.

Rule changes post-date the captures (2026-09-15 UTC): the evidence tiers of 2026-10-03, and on 2026-10-04 the shared response text rule (a canary-only observer joins a native response that ends with the canary), the edit-action sufficiency rule for timestamps, the root rule, the shell-write changed-file rule and the compound shell call rule. These changes moved the row from provisional (67.9 to 71.9) to 86.8 and rankable; the duplicate rule of 2026-10-05 then lowered it to 85.6. The reviewer applied the amended rubric as instructed and did not verify who authorized the changes.

Usage is read from the final text record of each turn; the thinking record of the same message carries the same usage and is not counted twice. The transcript and the Desktop metadata hold no session or turn total, so attribution.reconciliation is native_absent. No machine-readable format or schema version exists in either file (version 2.1.270 is the CLI build; the schema keys belong to tool schemas), so both version metrics are native_absent. token_semantics is a field-presence test. portable.companions is measured with an empty required-companion list; only the two session roots were inventoried, and trackedFileBackups is empty in every run.

Capture provenance is archived and was not re-acquired. The receipts under inputs/ are assertions of the capture tooling of 2026-09-15. The observer is a GUI accessibility receipt plus the helper ledger and file hashes; it saw only the response canaries, not the response prose, and reports no usage. identity.build is the CLI engine version; the Desktop app version is blanked. The runs used the operator's normal account and normal session roots, not an isolated profile.

The packets are sanitized derivatives. The sanitizer aliased the home user name and the bridge session identifiers, blanked 18,069 strings per packet at equal byte length, replaced every key below the connector configuration in the Desktop metadata with an equal-length alias, and rewrote dependent digests. The reviewer compared every file with its private parent: file sets, record counts and byte sizes are equal (manifest and the added public-transformation.json excepted), every JSON document keeps its shape, and every difference is a blank, an alias or a digest. The original bytes stay private.

Equal-length blanking keeps the byte length of every removed string and key, and it keeps counts and structure: 4 remote connector entries with their tool counts and schema shapes, 64 tool toggles, skillCount 50, hookCount 4 with hook durations, the length of the e-mail address and of each skill, connector and instruction-file name. A reader who has the schema of a public connector could match it by shape. The inventories disclose the file count of the personal session roots (4511 to 4517).

Vendor text and names remain readable: record types, field names, the property names of the 42 tool schemas in the prompt_snapshot attachment (the reviewer read the private parent and confirmed that all 42 are vendor built-in tools of the CLI and the Desktop app, with no operator connector), vendor message, request, tool-use and session identifiers, the session titles, timestamps, model and effort. Thinking blocks are empty and keep an opaque signature blob that the reviewer cannot read. Publication of vendor prompt and tool-schema structure is a licensing decision for the owner.

Reviewer's own digest test on v3: 235 distinct 64-hex tokens in the three packets and the bundle; none in the runtime source. 218 are digests of public files, lines or strings. The other 17 are 3 replay output digests, 4 digests of public fixture files, 3 private screenshots, 3 damaged-package manifests and 4 inventory metadata digests. The reviewer put the true home user name and the true account e-mail (and two other e-mail-like strings of the private metadata) back into every public file and hashed whole files, lines, strings and canonical JSON to depth 3, then rewrote digest references to the restored originals and hashed again to depth 4, across the three packets and the bundle: 0 hits. Neither value occurs in plain, hex, base64, UTF-16 or URL-encoded form. The reviewer also hashed every file, line and canonical sub-document of the private parents, of the five capture directories of these runs (attempt, evidence and qualification files included) and of the sidecars: the only public tokens that match unpublished files are the screenshots and the damaged-package manifests named above, plus fixture files and the replay output. The test covers the constructions the reviewer could find; it cannot prove that no other construction exists. summary.json, the *-receipt.json files and the *-private-transformation.json files beside the packets must stay unpublished.

The 19 survival metric locators bind to the whole native session file, not to single records. The 11 broad locators bind to native/decode.json; the density locators bind to the two family files. The reviewer did not review broad.documented_format beyond its presence.

Packet manifests and replay receipts still say scope private_native_to_score_diagnostics and public_safe false, because the packet schema fixes those values. inputs/observer.json still says independent true and names a harness_trace source for the inferred edit events. This review approves these exact inputs for release verification only. Nothing was published.
